classification.difficultyReason: Match ten exponential graphs using reflection, direction, intercepts and vertical translations.

inlines.text: Match the equation to the graph.

spec.sourceRegion: Graph a, first row, first column
spec.description: Positive decreasing exponential with two-ended axes and curve arrows; intercept 1. No grid, regular ticks or numerical axis range.
spec.mathematics: y=6^{-x}; horizontal asymptote y=0; y-intercept 1. Plot coordinates are an internal schematic frame, not additional givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Curve and intercept are supplied; matched equation is answer-only.

answer.worked: The curve decreases, has $y$-intercept $1$ and approaches $y=0$ from above to the right. Hence $y=6^{-x}$.

spec.sourceRegion: Graph b, first row, second column
spec.description: Decreasing curve below dashed asymptote 2, intercept 1, crossing the x-axis on the right. Two-ended axis and curve arrows; no regular ticks or grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Curve, asymptote and intercept are supplied; matched equation is answer-only.

answer.worked: The asymptote is $y=2$. The curve lies below it and decreases, so it is a reflected growth curve shifted up $2$. At $x=0$, $y=-1+2=1$, matching the intercept. Hence $y=-6^x+2$.

spec.sourceRegion: Graph c, first row, third column
spec.description: Increasing positive exponential, intercept 1, approaching the x-axis on the left. Both axes and curve have two end arrows; no grid or regular ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: Curve and intercept are supplied; matched equation is answer-only.

answer.worked: The curve increases, has $y$-intercept $1$ and approaches $y=0$ from above to the left. Hence $y=6^x$.

spec.sourceRegion: Graph d, first row, fourth column
spec.description: Increasing negative exponential, intercept -1, approaching the x-axis from below to the right. Two-ended axes and curve arrows; no regular ticks or grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Curve and intercept are supplied; matched equation is answer-only.

answer.worked: Reflecting $y=6^{-x}$ across the $x$-axis gives an increasing curve below $y=0$ with $y$-intercept $-1$. Hence $y=-6^{-x}$.

spec.sourceRegion: Graph e, second row, first column
spec.description: Decreasing negative exponential, intercept -1, approaching the x-axis from below on the left. Two-ended axes and curve arrows; no regular ticks or grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Curve and intercept are supplied; matched equation is answer-only.

answer.worked: Reflecting $y=6^x$ across the $x$-axis gives a decreasing curve below $y=0$ with $y$-intercept $-1$. Hence $y=-6^x$.

spec.sourceRegion: Graph f, second row, second column
spec.description: Decreasing curve above dashed asymptote -2, intercept -1, crossing the x-axis on the left. Two-ended axis and curve arrows; no grid or regular ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: Curve, asymptote and intercept are supplied; matched equation is answer-only.

answer.worked: The curve decreases above the asymptote $y=-2$, so it is $y=6^{-x}$ shifted down $2$. At $x=0$, $y=1-2=-1$, matching the intercept. Hence $y=6^{-x}-2$.

spec.sourceRegion: Graph g, second row, third column
spec.description: Increasing curve below dashed asymptote 2, intercept 1, crossing the x-axis on the left. Two-ended axes and curve arrows; no grid or regular ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: Curve, asymptote and intercept are supplied; matched equation is answer-only.

answer.worked: The curve increases below the asymptote $y=2$. Reflect $y=6^{-x}$ across the $x$-axis and shift it up $2$. At $x=0$, $y=-1+2=1$, matching the intercept. Hence $y=-6^{-x}+2$.

spec.sourceRegion: Graph h, second row, fourth column
spec.description: Increasing curve below dashed asymptote -2, intercept -3, falling to the left. Two-ended axes and curve arrows; no grid or regular ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: Curve, asymptote and intercept are supplied; matched equation is answer-only.

answer.worked: The curve increases below the asymptote $y=-2$. Reflect $y=6^{-x}$ across the $x$-axis and shift it down $2$. At $x=0$, $y=-1-2=-3$, matching the intercept. Hence $y=-6^{-x}-2$.

spec.sourceRegion: Graph i, third row, first column
spec.description: Decreasing curve below dashed asymptote -2, intercept -3, falling to the right. Two-ended axes and curve arrows; no grid or regular ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: Curve, asymptote and intercept are supplied; matched equation is answer-only.

answer.worked: The curve decreases below the asymptote $y=-2$. Reflect $y=6^x$ across the $x$-axis and shift it down $2$. At $x=0$, $y=-1-2=-3$, matching the intercept. Hence $y=-6^x-2$.

spec.sourceRegion: Graph j, third row, second column
spec.description: Decreasing curve above dashed asymptote 2, intercept 3, rising to the left. Two-ended axes and curve arrows; no grid or regular ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: Curve, asymptote and intercept are supplied; matched equation is answer-only.

answer.worked: The curve decreases above the asymptote $y=2$, so it is $y=6^{-x}$ shifted up $2$. At $x=0$, $y=1+2=3$, matching the intercept. Hence $y=6^{-x}+2$.
